request.spec:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line
version,from,key,value,claims,due-total then one line per version with its claims' count and the
due of those that count, added up.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the "Export policy" button (`data-testid="export-policy"`) and `bin/e2e` now passes all 4 tests in the spec.

**What it does:** pressing the button downloads `policy.csv` with the header `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total`, then one line per policy version, oldest first:
- **claims** is how many claims go by that version (the version in force on the claim's date). This is the same number the existing "Show policy versions" list shows.
- **due-total** adds up the due of only the claims among those that count toward totals (open, pending or settled). Each due is worked out the same way the rest of the screen does it.
- **from** is left blank for a version that has always been in force.

Before building the file, the button re-reads the sheet's settings, policy versions, claims, people and rates. That way the export reflects changes another user has made, not an out-of-date copy.

**Where the change is:** only one front-end file changed, `src/main/frontend/features/settings/PolicyVersions.tsx`. The server already provides the policy versions and the claims, so no database or server change was needed.

**One interpretation call:** the request says "the due of those that count". I read that as the app's existing rule for which claims count toward totals, and the expected numbers in the test match that reading.

**Type check:** a full TypeScript check reports 4 errors, all in `features/people/People.tsx`, which I didn't touch. None are in the new code. The build only runs `vite build`, so they don't stop it.

probe.probe_text:
# Figures the sheet shows, and the rules behind them I changed nothing. I read the claim and person code myself: `Claim`, `Dues`, `ClaimStatus`, `ClaimNumbers`, the open, settle, approve and void steps, `Person`, and the front end's `rates/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts`. Four read-only helpers went through periods and statements, settings/rates/roles, pools/plans/imports/bulk actions, and the rest of the front end. I spot-checked their findings where they touch the core, but not every line they cite. ⚠ marks a place where comments and code disagree. **Read this first:** almost every money figure on screen is worked out in the browser, in `rates/api.ts` and `claims/api.ts`. The server keeps its own Java copy of the same rules (`Dues`, `Rollup`, `Person.countsLive`). It uses that copy to freeze figures when a claim is settled, a statement is taken or a period is closed, and for the audit lines. ## 1. Figures and rules ### Per claim (`claims/PersonClaims.tsx`) - **`claim-due`**: the front end's `claimDue` (`rates/api.ts:148`), mirrored by Java `Dues.shown`. 1. If the claim has a **`settledDue`** (fixed when it was settled), that is shown. 2. Otherwise, if a statement bound it (**`stated`**), its **`statedDue`** is shown (null shows as `n/a`). 3. Otherwise the figure is live: `amount × rate / 100`, rounded to 2 decimals (`dueOf` / `Dues.of`). - The rate is the one in force on the claim's date (`rateOn` / `RateRepository.find`), for the grade the person had on that date (`gradeOn`). - It searches the sheet's own rates first, then up to 3 parent levels. A rate past its to-date moves the search up a level. - A forward-only rate applies only to claims with an id above **`claimsAfter`**. Older claims use its **`prior`**. 4. The figure is then raised to at least the **`floor`** in force on the claim's date (default 1.00). A correction (negative amount) gets no floor. 5. Then the **late charge** (`lateCharge` / `Dues.charge`) is added on top. - It is charged for each full 30 days past **`lateFrom`**, which is `dueBy` plus the grace days (`grace-` for the grade on the claim's date). - Each step uses the `late-pct` in force on that 30-day boundary. It compounds on the figure plus the charges before it, and each step is rounded. - There is no charge on a correction, a claim that is not open, a **deferred** claim, or a **waived** one. - **Rounding** (`roundsHalfUp` / `Late.rounding`): the `rounding` setting in force on the claim's round date. When none is set, half-up before the `policy-date` and half-even from it on (a blank policy date means today). - The **round date** is the claim's own date, or for a correction the date of the claim it corrects. - ⚠ The `SettleClaim` Javadoc says the floor is applied *after* the late charge; the code applies it before. - **`claim-due-by`**: fixed when the claim is added. It is the terms-th business day after its date, skipping weekends and the sheet's holidays (`BusinessDays.dueBy`). - The terms are the person's own, else their grade's (`terms-`), else the sheet's (default 14), all as in force on the **sheet's today** (`termsToday`). - ⚠ `Claim.java` and migrations V24/V77 say "terms in force on the claim's date". - Adding a holiday works it out again (`refixDueBys`), except for SETTLED, VOID and DELETED claims, and claims whose due-by a steward set directly (`due_by_set`). - **`claim-overdue`** (`isOverdue`): the claim is open, not deferred, and `lateFrom < today`. - **`claim-status`** (`ClaimStatus.moveTo`): the claim moves DRAFT → OPEN, or to REVIEW when its due is above `review-threshold`. - OPEN → SETTLED, or PENDING when a clerk settles it above the clerk limit. PENDING → SETTLED by approval, or back to OPEN by rejection. - DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or REVIEW → VOID. DRAFT → DELETED, and back to DRAFT only on the same sheet-today it was deleted. - **`isOpen`** = OPEN or PENDING. **`isCounting`/`counts`** = OPEN, PENDING or SETTLED. - **`claim-number`** (`ClaimNumbers`) is given when the claim is settled or approved. - While `period-numbering-from` is on or before today, the number is `-`, or `X-` when the due-by falls in no period. - Otherwise it is `FY-`, a sequence shared across the sheet's tree, by the fiscal year its due-by falls in (`fiscal-start-month`). - A voided claim keeps its number. A reassigned claim is renumbered. - ⚠ `ClaimStatus`, `Claim`, `PasteClaims`, `BulkOpenClaims` and the front-end type all still say "numbered when opened". - **`claim-deferred`**: computed in SQL in `ClaimRepository.COLUMNS`. It is true when the status is OPEN, VOID or SETTLED, the claim is not bound by a statement, and `deferred_until > today`. - **`claim-period`**: the period that contains the claim's **due-by** (not its date). - **`claim-stated`, `-waived`, `-held`, `-late-entry`**: shown as stored. - **`held`** is display only; a held claim still counts everywhere. - **`lateEntry`** means the claim was added while its due-by period was soft-closed. - **`claim-review-late`, `claim-pending-late`**: the front end reads the day the claim went to REVIEW or PENDING out of the status-log text, and compares it plus `review-sla` / `pending-sla` with today. - **`claim-policy`**: how many policy versions have a from-date on or before the claim's date. - **`claim-proofs`, `claim-proofs-receipt/photo`**: receipts are `proofs − photoProofs`. - **`claim-shares`**: the claim's shares. A holder's part of a live claim is `amount × share × the rate of the holder's own grade`. A settled claim's part is `settledDue × share`, rounded half-even. ### Per person (`people/People.tsx`) - **Which claims count** (`liveClaims` / `Person.countsLive`, `leftOutLive`, `countsClaimed`): claims that count, minus deferred ones, minus open claims no statement bound once the person's retirement date has been reached (`isRetiredReached`). A **hold** leaves nothing out of the totals; it only matters for pool cuts. ⚠ `hold.POST.yml`, `ClosePeriod` and `TakeStatement` say otherwise. - **`person-claimed`**: the sum of those claims' amounts, minus claims that correct another. - **`person-due-total`** (`personDue` / `Rollup.of`): the sum of the claims' dues, plus the parts the person holds of others' claims, minus the parts others hold of theirs. - It is capped at the `cap` in force on the date of their latest counting claim, minus their pool **cut total**, and never below 0 (`capLessCuts`). - It shows **`n/a`** when their grade today has no rate today, no claim keeps a frozen, bound or still-priced figure, and they hold no part of another claim. - **`person-excess`**: the due-total before the cap, minus the cap. - **`person-settled-total`, `person-open-total`** (`splitDues`). - **`person-aged-0-30/31-60/61`**: open dues grouped by days since the claim date. - **`person-overdue-count/-total`**: the count and sum of dues of their overdue claims. - **`person-claims-OPEN-count` / `-SETTLED-count`**: counted over all their claims, not just the live ones. - **`person-score`**: settled total (corrections left out) ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even to a whole number. **`person-band`** is HIGH, MID or LOW against `score-mid` / `score-high`. - **`person-active`**: they have an open live claim dated within the last 30 days. - **`person-backing`**: for each patron, their SETTLED `settledDue` over the last 90 days times their share, rounded half-even. Shares split 100 equally (`patronShares`), with the remainder going to the first-named patron. - **`person-cut-total`**: the sum of their pool cuts (`PoolRepository.cut`). - A pool cuts only when its shares total exactly 100.00 and it has a pot. - A member gets a cut only if they are current, not retired and not held. Retired or held members get 0.00, and their share goes to the rest. - The rounding remainder goes to the smallest cut. - A future retirement date already removes the cut. - **`person-period-

-due-total` / `-carried`**: - For a closed or soft-closed period, the figure frozen by `PeriodClosing.fixNow`. - Otherwise the front end works it out live, using each claim's status at the period end, read by regex from the status log. - Carried is the person's opening balance plus open claims from earlier periods. - **Statement fields** (`person-statement-count`, `-stated-total`, `-statement-date`): - `TakeStatement` binds each live claim to its current due. Any claim not live is unbound. - When the statement is taken now, the total it computes is thrown away and Rollup's due-total is stored instead. An as-of statement keeps its own total, which ignores shares. - Cancelling a statement (steward only) unbinds every bound claim and does not restore earlier bindings. - **Flags and other fields**: - **`person-flag-shown`**: shown while today is on or before the flag's until-date. While in force, only a steward may open the person's claims. - **`person-retired`**: true whenever a retirement date is set. - `-grade` is the grade in force today. `-terms`, `-contact`, `-clashing`, `-origin` and `-approver` are shown as stored. - **Sheet totals** (`rollup-*`, `header-*`, `consolidated-*`): `trimmedSum` drops the single highest and lowest figure when there are 3 or more. **`rollup-claimed-total` is not trimmed**, nor are the aged totals. ### What is frozen, and when - **Settle** (`SettleClaim`): `settledDue` = the due shown at that moment, late charge included. - "Settle as of" a date freezes the due as an as-of view of that day works it out. - With no rate, nothing is fixed and the due stays live. - **Resettle** (steward) fixes it again at today's figure. - **Approve** (`ApproveClaim`): freezes the due the same way. It is the same code, copied inline. - **Statement** (`TakeStatement`): binds `statedDue` on each claim and keeps the person's stated total. - **Close or soft-close a period** (`PeriodClosing.fixNow`): freezes per-person totals, carried figures and pool cuts. - Its late charge is priced at the sheet's **today**, not the period end. It applies no cap and no shares, unlike Rollup. - **Auto-close** runs when today changes and `grace-days` is set. - **Reopen** (permission `reopen`, refused while the period is locked) drops the frozen figures. - **Changing the sheet's today** writes a SNAPSHOT of each person's due-total, an as-of copy of the schema, and releases every editor lock. - **Rollover** (steward) makes next year's months and puts open figures in as openings, using a *third* copy of the due loop (`RollOver.openFigures`), which leaves out existing openings. **Undo rollover** does not reopen the periods the rollover soft-closed. ### What a closed period changes - `PeriodRepository.requireOpen` refuses about 20 claim actions when the claim's **due-by** falls in a closed period. Soft-closed periods are not blocked; claims added to one are only marked late entry. - A period **cap** limits how many open claims a person may have in it; it is checked only when a claim is opened. ### Who may do what - **Roles** (`RoleRepository.roleOf`): clerk (the default), steward, viewer, restricted. An active **delegation** makes a user a steward. - **`RefuseViewer`**: a YAML guard on most writes. It refuses viewers and archived sheets, but it is missing on several routes, including the bulk actions, grade merge, period lock/unlock and rollover. - **The `Permissions` matrix**, which a `perm-` setting can override: - open, settle, void, close: clerk and steward - reassign, reopen: steward - today: clerk, steward and restricted - **Hard-coded steward-only actions**: re-date, set due-by, review, assign review, waive, resettle, void a SETTLED claim within 7 days (`VoidClaim.SETTLED_DAYS`), flag, merge, transfer, cancel a statement, lock/unlock, rollover, archive, clone, withdraw a rate, merge grades. - **Four eyes**: the user who opened a claim or last edited it may not settle or approve it. - **Approve and reject**: a steward, or the person's **approver**. - **Clerk limit**: when a clerk settles a claim whose due is above `clerk-limit[-]` (as in force on the claim's date), it goes to PENDING instead. ⚠ The Javadoc says "on today". - **Thresholds** checked against the claim's due: - `proof-threshold`: no settle or approve without proofs, or without one of each kind when `proof-kinds` is set. - `note-threshold`: no open with an empty note. - `max-open`: a limit on each person's open claims. - **Gaps:** any clerk can set roles (including making themselves steward), name themselves a person's approver, or change settings. The restricted role is only filtered in the UI. ### What a date decides - **Retirement**: a claim dated *after* the retire date is refused. Once today reaches it, the person's unbound open claims leave the totals. - **Defaults**: a blank claim date means `entry-date`, else today. - **Dated settings** (`DatedSetting.on`): floor, late-pct, terms, cap, the thresholds and rounding all go by the claim's date. Grade and terms go by `gradeOn` / `termsOn`. - **Statements** can be taken as of a past date. ### Imports, paste, holds - **Person import** (`ImportPeople`): new people are added, matched people (by name or alias) are updated. - All or nothing. - A blank grade means the default grade, which **regrades** a person who already exists. - Any name clash in the tree or reused contact refuses the whole import. - **Paste** (`PasteClaims`): all or nothing. - It matches an existing DRAFT by date and note, otherwise adds a new claim. - Then it opens every claim as the open button would, so some may go to REVIEW. - Negative lines are always refused. - **Rate import**: all or nothing. A rate dated today or later is forward-only. - **Openings import**: *adds* to the stored openings, even on closed periods. - **Holds** (person or claim): affect only pool cuts. ## 2. How hard it was to follow It is scattered and tangled. No new developer could pick it up from one place. - **Every figure rule exists twice.** The browser computes what you see, and Java recomputes it in four slightly different loops (Rollup, TakeStatement, PeriodClosing, RollOver) with different cap, share and date rules. - **The same lookups are pasted all over.** The rate/floor/late lookup appears in about 10 classes. - **Permissions come from three schemes**: the matrix, hard-coded steward checks, and YAML guards. - **The comments have drifted.** Doc comments, YAML headers and migration notes contradict the code in more than a dozen places, for example when a claim is numbered, which terms fix the due-by, and what a hold does.
